newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares succumbed to heavy profit taking on Wednesday as investors to their cue from a soft York market and set of weaker than expected results at home to cash in on the bourse's steep rise so far this year.

The AEX index of leading shares ended 14.79 points lower at 759.41, a loss of 1.91 percent. But dealers said the fall should be taken in the context of rather thin volume and that the index has climbed around 100 points in the last six weeks.
The domestic cue for today's profit-taking came from pre-bourse earnings announcements from Anglo-Dutch publisher Reed-Elsevier and then brewer Grolsch.
"We've come a long way in a pretty short time," said one dealer. "The figures gave a bit of extra momentum."
Reed-Elsevier announced 1996 pre-tax profits of 805 million stg, up 11 percent on the year before but below the main range forecast by analysts of 808 to 821 million.
"The results aren't that good but maybe the Dutch side will do better because of the currency factor," one dealer said.

Reed's dividend was raised by 11 percent to 27.2 pence per share but Elsevier's dividend was raised 29 percent to 0.76 guilders per share. It said this was a consequence of sterling's appreciation against the guilder.
The group said that if sterling remained strong this would have a negative effect on Reed's earnings per share in 1997 but a positive effect on Elsevier's earnings per share.
London-traded Reed International shares also lost ground but dealers said the differing outlook based on currency factors could in the future push the shares in different ways.
Elsevier shares topped the volume list and closed 1.30 guilders off at 31.20, up from an earlier low at 30.70 guilders.
Brewer Grolsch also reported pre-bourse, announcing 1996 net profits at the low end of forecasts at 59.9 million guilders, only just bettering the previous year's 58.8 million.
The shares tumbled to a close 15.00 guilders down, a fall of 20 percent, to 59.00 guilders. Dealers noted the company also said that 1997 profits would fail to match those of 1996.
"The results were bad but the outlook was even worse," one dealer said. "Pretty disappointing all round," said another.
Beer sector weakness spread to Heineken, in which investor jitters ahead of the company reporting on Friday caused the shares to crumble to close 20.80 guilders weaker at 317.20.
Another mover was chemicals giant Akzo Nobel, which suffered after German sector rival Hoechst plunged on plans not to list a subsidiary and issued a weak sales outlook for 1997.
Hoechst shares plunged over 10 percent after it said it would not list its HMR unit and 1997 group sales would drop to between 42 and 47 billion marks from 50.9 billion in 1996.
Akzo Nobel closed 11.10 guilders easier at 276.70 and fellow chemicals firm DSM fell to 7.30 to 191.00 guilders.
"The Hoechst news has taken its toll on the chemicals sector," one dealer said.

Elsewhere, weakness in the AEX index as a whole had an effect on banking groups ABN AMRO and ING. ABN AMRO finished 1.70 guilders down at 136.80 and ING slipped 2.00 to 78.00 guilders. -- Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
